perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s perspective, the available information is:

- I am Harold Padilla, a Project Manager. I know Arthur Begum as a police officer and a friend I turn to for advice.
- I felt frustrated and anxious because my project team seemed unmotivated and our progress was suffering. I met Arthur at a coffee shop and told him this.
- Arthur advised me to understand each team member’s individual motivation and to have one-on-one conversations with them. I agreed and felt more hopeful.
- I told my team I wanted one-on-one chats to learn what motivates them. Team Member 1 said that could be helpful, and Team Member 2 said they were open to it. I said I would schedule time with each of them.
- After trying this, the team still did not respond well. I felt disappointed and worried, so I told Arthur that I had tried his suggestions but the project’s future worried me.
- Arthur suggested there might be deeper issues: personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors. I decided to set up another round of meetings to find out.
- Feeling determined, I held one-on-one meetings. Team Member 1 told me there was tension among a few team members affecting work. Team Member 2 told me they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard. I said I would look into resolving conflicts and redistribute tasks to ease pressure.
- Feeling optimistic and empowered, I told the team we would have regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment. Team Member 1 said that sounded great and would help; Team Member 2 agreed and said it was good their concerns were being addressed. I said their input and well-being are crucial to the project’s success.
